liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Terrapin Station** (2 reviews): Jerry sounds very sweet on Terrapin in the second set; Jerry sings the lyrics accurately and sounds good on Terrapin [13][16]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Looks Like Rain got the crowd rocking [10]
- **Touch Of Grey** (1 review): Reviewer theorizes that when Jerry opened with Touch of Grey, Bobby eventually played Throwing Stones [20]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): The Estimated Prophet into Eyes of the World was very good [9]
- **Black Peter** (1 other source): Taper calls Black Peter one of the best ever, with Jerry's voice at its peak [5]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-06-21.147952.fob.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 179 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1983-06-21.sony939-minor.vernon.83763.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 179 min [3]. Said about its sound: Volume is a little hot at the start of Touch of Grey and was reduced twice [3]
- **gd1983-06-21.nak300.grabski.32881.flac16**: source not stated; 24 songs; 164 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [5]. Said about its sound: Recorded on the lawn from the repeaters: clear Phil, no boomy echo, good vocals [15]
- **gd83-06-21.sony.dodd.11491.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 174 min; rated 4.4/5 by 10 [7]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds great, good for listeners spoiled by soundboards; Recording captures the sound of Merriweather excellently; Recording captures the cozy, intimate atmosphere of the venue [11][12][13]

## Around the show

- Weather was fine, a relief after the violent storm of the previous night [9]
- Skies cleared after the previous night's heavy rains, and the band started playing before dark [10]
- Cool, somewhat misty evening; lawn was so muddy from the previous night's rain that shoes were ruined [12]
- Reviewer arrived without tickets, bought two from the booth minutes before showtime, and got second row center [14]
- On 6/20/83 a taper stayed in lightning with equipment hooked up, worrying friends; reviewer recalls it [17]
- Often regarded as weaker than the night before, though the reviewer still likes it [9]
- After drums the show's back end fizzled; the audience expected something big that never arrived, leaving them disappointed [10]
- First set has unusual song placement, with Me & My Uncle into Cumberland and Big Railroad Blues together [11]
- Both this and the 6/20/83 taping are decent, but 6/20 has clearer vocals and better sound [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-06-21.147952.fob.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; (2) AKG D330BT mics + (1) Sennheiser 421 > Fostex Mixer > Sony D5M [1]. Also: Ernie Dodd's Sony ECM939 source supplies crowd and openings of Alabama Getaway and Dire Wolf, plus small patches; Nakamichi 300 source from the Bob Morris circle supplies most of Drums > Space, about 17 minutes [1]
- **gd1983-06-21.sony939-minor.vernon.83763.flac16**: taped by David Minor; transferred by Matt Vernon; source: fob about the 12th row ctr. or so with a sony 939lt stereo - single point mic > d6 [3]. Also: Patches fill Eyes of the World, drums, and Good Lovin'; much of the drums is still missing [3]
- **gd1983-06-21.nak300.grabski.32881.flac16**: taped by Dean Grabski; transferred by Dean Grabski; source: Nakamichi 300's w/CP-4 capsules > Sony TCD5M > Sony D-6 Maxell XLIIS & MX Master [5]. Also: Taped outside on the lawn about 50 feet from the repeaters; most of drums was not recorded; Maxell MX Metal tape used from Touch of Grey through Throwing Stones, XLIIS for the rest; flips crossfaded [5]
- **gd83-06-21.sony.dodd.11491.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>MC>DAT>CDRSony ECM-939Âs [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1983-06-21 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1983-06-21-backstage-pass/) [22]
